concept: Cross-cutting: Prompting Techniques (reasoning, structured output, robustness, prompt optimization)
summary:
Prompting is the cross-cutting control surface for every other pipeline component: it determines how retrieval context is presented, how decomposition sub-tasks are specified, how verifiers are asked to judge, and what the cache keys look like. The verified literature establishes a small set of high-leverage facts. (1) Eliciting intermediate reasoning works: few-shot chain-of-thought (Wei et al., NeurIPS 2022) and zero-shot "Let's think step by step" (Kojima et al., NeurIPS 2022; MultiArith 17.7% -> 78.7%, GSM8K 10.4% -> 40.7% on text-davinci-002) are the foundations, and sampling-and-voting (self-consistency, Wang et al., ICLR 2023; +17.9 GSM8K, 5-10 paths capture most of the gain) remains the most reliable test-time compute multiplier for tasks with checkable final answers. (2) Prompts are brittle in ways that are not semantically meaningful: demonstration order alone moves accuracy from near-random to near-SOTA (Lu et al., ACL 2022), format-only edits move LLaMA-2-13B by up to 76 points (Sclar et al., ICLR 2024), label bias and recency bias dominate few-shot classification (Zhao et al., ICML 2021), demonstration labels matter less than input distribution, label space and format (Min et al., EMNLP 2022), information in the middle of a long context is under-used (Liu et al., TACL 2024; 22-point drop at 20 documents), and irrelevant context sharply degrades reasoning (Shi et al., ICML 2023). Persona/role prompts do not reliably improve objective accuracy (Zheng et al., Findings EMNLP 2024), and intrinsic self-correction without external signal can make answers worse (Huang et al., ICLR 2024). (3) The remedy for brittleness is to treat prompts as optimized, versioned artifacts rather than hand-tuned strings: APE (ICLR 2023), OPRO (ICLR 2024), DSPy (ICLR 2024 spotlight) with MIPRO (EMNLP 2024), and TextGrad (Nature 2025) all show that LLM-driven search over instructions and demonstrations against a held-out metric beats human prompt engineering, and the Prompt Report's own 20-hour human case study was beaten by a DSPy-compiled prompt (F1 0.548 vs 0.53). Compositions of simple techniques such as Medprompt (kNN few-shot + model-generated CoT + 5-way shuffled ensemble: MedQA 81.7% -> 90.2%) and Self-Discover (self-composed reasoning structures, up to +32% over CoT at 10-40x less compute than CoT-SC) are task-agnostic recipes that transfer across domains.

For frontier reasoning models the guidance has shifted: both Anthropic and OpenAI documentation now say to prefer general instructions over prescriptive step-by-step plans, to try zero-shot before adding examples, to use clear delimiters (XML tags), to place long documents before the query (Anthropic reports up to 30% better responses on complex multi-document inputs), and to avoid asking for explicit CoT in the output when native thinking is on. Structured output is now a decoding-time guarantee (constrained decoding on both Claude and OpenAI; OpenAI reports 100% schema adherence vs <40% for gpt-4-0613), but format restriction can degrade reasoning (Tam et al. 2024), so the dominant production pattern is "reason free-form, then emit schema" in two steps. Prompt injection remains unsolved at the model level (Greshake et al. 2023; Perez & Ribeiro 2022); defenses combine provenance marking of untrusted data (spotlighting cuts attack success from >50% to <2%), instruction hierarchies, and architectural isolation. Prompt compression (LLMLingua, EMNLP 2023, up to 20x; LLMLingua-2, Findings ACL 2024, 2-5x with 1.6-2.9x end-to-end speedup) is a cost lever that must be gated by evals because it interacts with the lost-in-the-middle and irrelevant-context failure modes.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Jason Wei, Xuezhi Wang, Dale Schuurmans, Maarten Bosma, Brian Ichter, Fei Xia, Ed Chi, Quoc Le, Denny Zhou
papers.citation_signal: Foundational; third-party aggregators list ~4,000-6,000 citations; Paper Digest ranks it the second most influential NeurIPS 2022 paper.
papers.key_contribution: Shows that a few exemplars that include intermediate reasoning steps elicit multi-step reasoning in sufficiently large models, with gains on arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic benchmarks across three model families. A 540B model with eight CoT exemplars reached state of the art on GSM8K, surpassing fine-tuned GPT-3 with a verifier. The ability is emergent with scale and absent in small models.
papers.design_implication: Reasoning should be elicited explicitly (via exemplars with rationales, a thinking instruction, or native thinking mode) for any non-trivial task. Few-shot CoT exemplars are an asset the component must manage (store, select, version). Because the effect is scale-dependent, the component should select technique by model tier rather than hard-code CoT everywhere.

papers.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
papers.authors: Takeshi Kojima, Shixiang Shane Gu, Machel Reid, Yutaka Matsuo, Yusuke Iwasawa
papers.citation_signal: Foundational zero-shot CoT paper, thousands of citations; its trigger phrase is quoted in essentially every later prompting paper and vendor doc.
papers.key_contribution: A single task-agnostic trigger, 'Let's think step by step', appended before the answer raises text-davinci-002 from 17.7% to 78.7% on MultiArith and 10.4% to 40.7% on GSM8K, with similar gains for PaLM 540B, across arithmetic, symbolic and logical tasks. Uses a two-stage prompt: reasoning extraction, then answer extraction with a second call.
papers.design_implication: Zero-shot CoT is the cheapest reasoning baseline and should be the default when no demonstrations exist. The two-stage pattern (reason, then extract answer) is the template for 'reason free-form then emit structured answer' used in production. Trigger phrases are tunable (see APE and OPRO, which found better ones).

papers.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
papers.authors: Xuezhi Wang, Jason Wei, Dale Schuurmans, Quoc Le, Ed Chi, Sharan Narang, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Denny Zhou
papers.citation_signal: Listed among Paper Digest's most influential ICLR 2023 papers; the canonical test-time-compute ensembling method, thousands of citations.
papers.key_contribution: Replace greedy CoT decoding with sampling many reasoning paths and majority-voting the final answer: +17.9 GSM8K, +11.0 SVAMP, +12.2 AQuA, +6.4 StrategyQA, +3.9 ARC-c. Main experiments used 40 samples (T=0.7, top-k 40 for PaLM-540B; T=0.5 for LaMDA/UL2); accuracy saturates quickly, with 5-10 paths capturing most of the gain. Robust to imperfect prompts (LaMDA GSM8K 14.9 greedy -> 23.4 with SC) and works with zero-shot CoT (PaLM GSM8K 43.0 -> 69.2).
papers.design_implication: Expose a 'samples' knob with default 5 (cheap) to 10 (quality), T about 0.7, and an answer-normalizer for voting. Use it only for tasks with an extractable final answer; use Universal Self-Consistency for free-form outputs. Gains are large enough that SC should be the first lever when accuracy matters more than cost; it composes with the parallelization component since samples are independent.

papers.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers (APE)
papers.authors: Yongchao Zhou, Andrei Ioan Muresanu, Ziwen Han, Keiran Paster, Silviu Pitis, Harris Chan, Jimmy Ba
papers.citation_signal: ICLR 2023 poster; first widely cited automatic instruction search method; its discovered CoT trigger is reused across the field.
papers.key_contribution: Treats the instruction as a program: an LLM proposes candidate instructions from input-output demos, a target LLM is scored on each (execution accuracy outperformed log-prob as the score), and the best is kept. Matches or beats human instructions on 24/24 Instruction Induction tasks and 17/21 BIG-Bench tasks. Default 50 candidates; performance reaches human level around 64; iterative Monte Carlo resampling helped only marginally (gains taper after about 3 rounds). Discovered 'Let's work this out in a step by step way to be sure we have the right answer' (MultiArith 82.0 vs 78.7, GSM8K 43.0 vs 40.7).
papers.design_implication: Implement a propose-score-select loop as the simplest prompt optimizer: 50-64 candidates, execution-accuracy metric on a held-out dev set, no iteration by default. Treat trigger phrases as searchable parameters per model and domain, not constants.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers (OPRO)
papers.authors: Chengrun Yang, Xuezhi Wang, Yifeng Lu, Hanxiao Liu, Quoc V. Le, Denny Zhou, Xinyun Chen
papers.citation_signal: ICLR 2024; widely adopted as the reference 'LLM as optimizer' method, hundreds of citations.
papers.key_contribution: The optimizer LLM sees a meta-prompt containing prior instructions with their scores (top 20 kept, ascending), 3 task exemplars, and generates 8 new instructions per step at T=1.0; the scorer runs at T=0 on a small training subset (3.5% of GSM8K, about 260 problems). Best prompt for PaLM 2-L: 'Take a deep breath and work on this problem step-by-step' at 80.2% GSM8K vs 71.8% for 'Let's think step by step' and 34.0% for no instruction. Up to +8% GSM8K and up to +50% on Big-Bench Hard over human prompts.
papers.design_implication: Score-conditioned trajectory optimization is a drop-in upgrade over APE: keep a bounded history of (instruction, score), sample at high temperature for proposals, score greedily on a small (hundreds) dev set to control cost, and evaluate on a disjoint test set to detect overfitting. Instructions found are model-specific; re-run when the underlying model changes.

papers.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines
papers.authors: Omar Khattab, Arnav Singhvi, Paridhi Maheshwari, Zhiyuan Zhang, Keshav Santhanam, Sri Vardhamanan, Saiful Haq, Ashutosh Sharma, Thomas T. Joshi, Hanna Moazam, Heather Miller, Matei Zaharia, Christopher Potts
papers.citation_signal: ICLR 2024 spotlight; the most widely used open-source prompt-compilation framework in industry (Stanford/Databricks lineage), with an active optimizer ecosystem.
papers.key_contribution: Models an LM pipeline as a text-transformation graph of declarative modules (signatures) whose prompts and demonstrations are parameters; a compiler bootstraps demonstrations by running the pipeline and keeping traces that pass a metric. GPT-3.5 and llama2-13b-chat compiled with DSPy outperform standard few-shot prompting by >25% and >65% and expert-written demonstrations by 5-46% and 16-40%; 770M T5 and llama2-13b compiled programs are competitive with expert GPT-3.5 prompt chains. Documentation guidance: ~10 examples -> BootstrapFewShot; 50+ -> BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch; 200+ and 40+ trials -> MIPROv2; typical run costs about $2 and ten minutes.
papers.design_implication: Separate the 'what' (signature: inputs, outputs, constraints) from the 'how' (instructions, demos, reasoning strategy) and make the 'how' compiled, versioned and re-compilable per model. This is the architectural backbone for a task-agnostic prompting component: every pipeline stage declares a signature and a metric, and the optimizer fills in the prompt.

papers.title: Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs (MIPRO)
papers.authors: Krista Opsahl-Ong, Michael J. Ryan, Josh Purtell, David Broman, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia, Omar Khattab
papers.citation_signal: EMNLP 2024 main; ships as DSPy's default optimizer (MIPROv2), so it has large real-world adoption.
papers.key_contribution: Jointly optimizes free-form instructions and few-shot demos for every module of a multi-stage program without module-level labels: grounded instruction proposal (task summary, data summary, program code, bootstrapped demos), a Bayesian surrogate learned from stochastic mini-batch evaluations, and meta-optimization of the proposer. With Llama-3-8B it beats baseline optimizers on 5 of 7 programs by up to 13% accuracy.
papers.design_implication: When a pipeline has several LLM stages, optimize them jointly against the end metric rather than stage by stage; use mini-batch evaluation plus a surrogate to keep cost bounded. Provide 'light/medium/heavy' budget presets so teams can trade optimization cost for quality.

papers.title: TextGrad: Automatic 'Differentiation' via Text (journal version: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback)
papers.authors: Mert Yuksekgonul, Federico Bianchi, Joseph Boen, Sheng Liu, Pan Lu, Zhi Huang, Carlos Guestrin, James Zou
papers.citation_signal: Published in Nature (DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-08661-4); PyTorch-style open-source framework with broad uptake.
papers.key_contribution: Backpropagates natural-language critiques ('textual gradients') through a compound system's computation graph to improve prompts, code, molecules or treatment plans; user supplies only an objective. Raised GPT-4o zero-shot GPQA from 51% to 55%, gave about 20% relative gain on LeetCode-Hard, and produced improved reasoning prompts.
papers.design_implication: For stages whose outputs are judged by an LLM critic rather than exact match (specs, incident write-ups, design rationales), use feedback-driven optimization: a critic prompt produces structured critiques that an editor prompt applies to the instruction. Keep the critic and editor as separate signatures so the same loop can optimize any node in the pipeline.

papers.title: The Prompt Report: A Systematic Survey of Prompt Engineering Techniques
papers.authors: Sander Schulhoff, Michael Ilie, Nishant Balepur, et al. (31 authors)
papers.citation_signal: Most comprehensive prompting survey to date (33 terms, 58 text techniques, 40 multimodal); widely cited by vendors, practitioners and follow-up surveys.
papers.key_contribution: Taxonomy of 58 text prompting techniques grouped into In-Context Learning, Thought Generation, Decomposition, Ensembling, Self-Criticism and Zero-Shot families. MMLU benchmark on gpt-3.5-turbo (2,800 questions): few-shot CoT performed best; zero-shot CoT was worse than plain zero-shot; self-consistency (3 runs, T=0.5) helped only zero-shot prompts; choosing a technique is 'like hyperparameter search'. Case study: a human prompt engineer spent 47 steps / ~20 hours to reach F1 0.53 on suicidal-crisis entrapment detection and found unexplained sensitivities (duplicated email text raised F1; removing it cost 0.07; anonymizing names cost 0.08); a DSPy-optimized prompt reached test F1 0.548.
papers.design_implication: Use the taxonomy as the component's technique registry (each family is a pluggable strategy). Never assume a technique helps: the benchmark shows zero-shot CoT can hurt on some model/task pairs, so technique selection must be eval-driven. Budget for automated optimization instead of long manual iteration.

papers.title: Principled Instructions Are All You Need for Questioning LLaMA-1/2, GPT-3.5/4
papers.authors: Sondos Mahmoud Bsharat, Aidar Myrzakhan, Zhiqiang Shen
papers.citation_signal: Widely circulated practitioner reference (the '26 principles'); hundreds of citations and many industry summaries.
papers.key_contribution: 26 instruction-design principles (audience specification, role assignment, 'Your task is'/'You MUST', delimiters, few-shot, output primers, step-by-step, bias disclaimers, etc.) evaluated on ATLAS with LLaMA-1/2 7B-70B and GPT-3.5/4. Reported ~57.7% average quality ('boosting') improvement and 36.4% correctness improvement on GPT-4; about a stable 50% quality gain across models; correctness gains >10% on average and >20% for larger models, growing with model size.
papers.design_implication: Encode these principles as a linter/normalizer that runs over any natural-language task prompt before execution (ensure audience, explicit task statement, delimiters, output format primer). Treat the gimmicky ones (tipping, penalties) as optional flags to be A/B tested, not defaults, since their evaluation relied partly on LLM-judged quality.

papers.title: Can Generalist Foundation Models Outcompete Special-Purpose Tuning? Case Study in Medicine (Medprompt)
papers.authors: Harsha Nori, Yin Tat Lee, Sheng Zhang, Dean Carignan, Richard Edgar, Nicolo Fusi, Nicholas King, Jonathan Larson, Yuanzhi Li, Weishung Liu, Renqian Luo, Scott Mayer McKinney, Robert Osazuwa Ness, Hoifung Poon, Tao Qin, Naoto Usuyama, Chris White, Eric Horvitz
papers.venue: arXiv (Microsoft Research); companion blog 'The Power of Prompting'
papers.citation_signal: Hundreds of citations; defined the 'composed prompting beats fine-tuning' narrative and is reused in Microsoft's later o1/Medprompt follow-ups.
papers.key_contribution: Composition of three domain-agnostic steps: kNN-selected few-shot examples (embedding similarity), GPT-4 self-generated CoT rationales for those examples, and an ensemble with shuffled answer choices. MedQA ablation: zero-shot 81.7 -> random few-shot 83.9 -> +CoT 87.3 -> kNN few-shot 88.4 -> shuffled ensemble 90.2; SOTA on all nine MultiMedQA datasets; 27% error reduction vs Med-PaLM 2 with about an order of magnitude fewer calls; transfers to electrical engineering, ML, law, accounting, nursing exams.
papers.design_implication: The canonical task-agnostic recipe: retrieve similar solved examples, generate rationales once and cache them, ensemble with order perturbation to cancel position bias. Each stage is independently toggleable so the component can run the cheap subset (kNN + CoT) by default and enable the 5-way ensemble only when accuracy targets require it.

papers.title: Self-Discover: Large Language Models Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
papers.authors: Pei Zhou, Jay Pujara, Xiang Ren, Xinyun Chen, Heng-Tze Cheng, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Swaroop Mishra, Huaixiu Steven Zheng
papers.citation_signal: NeurIPS 2024; Google DeepMind; frequently cited as the compute-efficient alternative to CoT-SC.
papers.key_contribution: Stage 1 (once per task): the model SELECTs from 39 atomic reasoning modules, ADAPTs them to the task, and IMPLEMENTs a JSON reasoning structure. Stage 2: every instance is solved by following that structure. Up to +32% over CoT for GPT-4 and PaLM 2 on BBH, grounded agent reasoning (T4D) and MATH; >20% better than CoT-Self-Consistency at 10-40x less inference compute; structures transfer PaLM 2-L -> GPT-4 -> Llama2.
papers.design_implication: When a task prompt arrives, run a one-time planning call that produces a reasoning structure (a JSON skeleton of steps), cache it keyed by task signature, and reuse it for every instance. This is how the component 'reasons about how to execute' a task without paying per-instance planning cost.

papers.title: Meta-Prompting: Enhancing Language Models with Task-Agnostic Scaffolding
papers.authors: Mirac Suzgun, Adam Tauman Kalai
papers.citation_signal: Widely discussed task-agnostic scaffolding paper; influential on orchestrator/expert agent designs.
papers.key_contribution: A single model acts as a 'conductor' that decomposes the task, spins up fresh expert instances of the same model with tailored instructions, integrates and verifies their outputs, optionally calling a Python interpreter. On Game of 24, Checkmate-in-One and Python Programming Puzzles with GPT-4, it beats standard prompting by 17.1%, expert (dynamic) prompting by 17.3% and multipersona prompting by 15.2%.
papers.design_implication: Implement the conductor pattern as the component's orchestration mode: the conductor prompt is task-agnostic, expert prompts are generated per sub-task, and a verification step is mandatory before the final answer. Fresh-context experts avoid cross-contamination and map directly onto the parallelization component.

papers.title: Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
papers.authors: Sewon Min, Xinxi Lyu, Ari Holtzman, Mikel Artetxe, Mike Lewis, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Luke Zettlemoyer
papers.citation_signal: EMNLP 2022; a foundational analysis of in-context learning with well over a thousand citations.
papers.key_contribution: Across 12 models including GPT-3, randomly replacing demonstration labels barely hurts classification and multiple-choice performance; what matters is exposure to the label space, the input-text distribution, and the sequence format.
papers.design_implication: Demonstration selection should prioritize format fidelity and coverage of the input distribution and label space over perfect gold labels, which means synthetic or weakly labeled exemplars are acceptable for format-steering. For engineering domains, use real in-domain inputs (log lines, requirement sentences) even when outputs are model-generated.

papers.title: Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them: Overcoming Few-Shot Prompt Order Sensitivity
papers.authors: Yao Lu, Max Bartolo, Alastair Moore, Sebastian Riedel, Pontus Stenetorp
papers.citation_signal: ACL 2022; the standard reference for demonstration-order sensitivity, over a thousand citations.
papers.key_contribution: The order of the same few-shot examples moves GPT-family accuracy from near-random to near-SOTA; the effect holds across sizes, is not tied to particular examples and does not transfer across models. Generating an artificial dev set with the model itself and ranking permutations by entropy statistics yields a 13% relative improvement across eleven classification tasks.
papers.design_implication: Never accept an arbitrary demo order. Either fix the order via a probing-set entropy heuristic (no labels required) or neutralize it by ensembling over permutations (as Medprompt does). Pin and version the chosen order per model; re-select on model upgrade.

papers.title: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
papers.authors: Tony Z. Zhao, Eric Wallace, Shi Feng, Dan Klein, Sameer Singh
papers.citation_signal: ICML 2021; foundational analysis of few-shot instability, >1,500 citations.
papers.key_contribution: Few-shot GPT-3 accuracy swings from chance to SOTA with prompt format, example choice and order because of bias toward answers that are recent in the prompt or common in pretraining. Contextual calibration (query with a content-free input such as 'N/A', fit affine parameters so that prediction is uniform) raises average accuracy by up to 30 points and reduces variance.
papers.design_implication: For classification-style stages (triage, severity labels, pass/fail), add a calibration step using content-free probes when logprobs are available, or balance and shuffle label order when they are not. Log per-label priors as a drift signal.

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.authors: Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, Percy Liang
papers.citation_signal: TACL; one of the most cited LLM papers of 2023, replicated on later frontier models and the basis of vendor long-context guidance.
papers.key_contribution: U-shaped position curve: with 20 retrieved documents, GPT-3.5-Turbo scored 75.8% when the gold document was first, 53.8% at position 9 and 63.2% last; the worst case falls below the 56.1% closed-book baseline. More documents hurt (worst-middle 61.2 -> 53.8 -> 50.5 for 10/20/30). Query-aware contextualization (query before and after) nearly solved synthetic key-value retrieval but barely helped QA. Reader accuracy saturates around 20 documents (+1.5 points from 20 to 50).
papers.design_implication: The prompting component owns context layout: place the highest-ranked evidence first and last, keep k around 10-20 passages, repeat the query after the documents, and prefer reranking over stuffing. This is the direct interface contract with the hybrid retrieval and RAG components.

papers.title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
papers.authors: Freda Shi, Xinyun Chen, Kanishka Misra, Nathan Scales, David Dohan, Ed Chi, Nathanael Schärli, Denny Zhou
papers.citation_signal: ICML 2023; standard citation for distractor sensitivity in RAG and agent contexts.
papers.key_contribution: On GSM-IC (GSM8K with irrelevant sentences), accuracy of state-of-the-art prompting methods drops dramatically; self-consistency and an explicit instruction to ignore irrelevant information mitigate the drop.
papers.design_implication: Include an explicit 'ignore irrelevant material; use only what is needed' instruction in any prompt that receives retrieved or tool-generated context, and gate how much context is injected. Combine with quote-first grounding so the model filters before reasoning.

papers.title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (FormatSpread)
papers.authors: Melanie Sclar, Yejin Choi, Yulia Tsvetkov, Alane Suhr
papers.citation_signal: ICLR 2024; the reference work on formatting sensitivity, adopted by evaluation frameworks.
papers.key_contribution: Semantically equivalent format changes (separators, spacing, casing, enumeration style) produce spreads of up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B and up to 56 for GPT-3.5 (median 6.4 across 53 tasks); median 7.5 points with only 10 sampled formats; removing one colon moved a task from 0.043 to 0.826. Sensitivity persists with scale, more shots and instruction tuning; format rankings correlate weakly across models. FormatSpread uses Thompson-sampling bandit search to estimate the interval cheaply.
papers.design_implication: Report evals as intervals across formats, not single numbers. Freeze a canonical prompt template per model and treat any whitespace or delimiter edit as a code change requiring re-evaluation. Format search (10-20 variants) is a cheap optimizer to run before instruction search.

papers.title: When 'A Helpful Assistant' Is Not Really Helpful: Personas in System Prompts Do Not Improve Performances of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Mingqian Zheng, Jiaxin Pei, Lajanugen Logeswaran, Moontae Lee, David Jurgens
papers.citation_signal: Findings of EMNLP 2024; the most-cited empirical test of role prompting, widely referenced in vendor guidance debates.
papers.key_contribution: 162 personas across 4 LLM families on 2,410 factual questions: adding a persona does not improve accuracy over a no-persona control; effects depend unpredictably on gender, type and domain; the best persona per question would help, but automatic persona selection performs about as well as random.
papers.design_implication: Use system-prompt roles for tone, scope and format control, not as an accuracy lever. The component should not spend optimization budget on persona search; spend it on instructions, demonstrations and context layout instead.

papers.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
papers.authors: Jie Huang, Xinyun Chen, Swaroop Mishra, Huaixiu Steven Zheng, Adams Wei Yu, Xinying Song, Denny Zhou
papers.citation_signal: ICLR 2024; the standard caution against naive 'reflect and fix' loops.
papers.key_contribution: Intrinsic self-correction (asking the model to review and revise its own reasoning without external feedback) does not improve reasoning benchmarks and sometimes degrades them; gains reported elsewhere depended on oracle labels.
papers.design_implication: Any self-check prompt must be grounded in external signal: test results, schema validation, retrieved evidence, a tool execution, or an independent verifier with different context. Do not ship 'please double-check your answer' loops as a verification strategy on their own.

papers.title: What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3?
papers.authors: Jiachang Liu, Dinghan Shen, Yizhe Zhang, Bill Dolan, Lawrence Carin, Weizhu Chen
papers.citation_signal: Over a thousand citations; the origin of retrieval-based (kNN) demonstration selection used by Medprompt and DSPy KNNFewShot.
papers.key_contribution: Retrieving demonstrations semantically similar to the test input (sentence-embedding kNN) consistently beats random selection across NLU and NLG benchmarks, with large gains on ToTTo table-to-text (about 44%) and NQ open-domain QA (45.5%); task-tuned encoders retrieve even better examples.
papers.design_implication: Maintain an exemplar store with embeddings; at inference, retrieve the top-k (3-5) most similar solved examples for the few-shot block. This unifies the demonstration selector with the hybrid retrieval component (same index technology, different corpus).

papers.title: Many-Shot In-Context Learning
papers.authors: Rishabh Agarwal, Avi Singh, Lei M. Zhang, Bernd Bohnet, Luis Rosias, Stephanie Chan, et al.
papers.citation_signal: NeurIPS 2024 spotlight; Google DeepMind; defines the long-context ICL regime.
papers.key_contribution: With hundreds to thousands of in-context examples, performance keeps improving on many tasks, can override pretraining biases and approaches fine-tuning. Reinforced ICL (model-generated rationales filtered by correctness) and Unsupervised ICL (inputs only) remove the need for human rationales. Cost scales linearly with shots.
papers.design_implication: When a long-context model and a cached prefix are available, the component can scale the demonstration block far beyond 5 shots; combine with prompt caching so the many-shot prefix is paid once. Generate rationales automatically and filter by metric, as in Medprompt and DSPy bootstrapping.

papers.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Huiqiang Jiang, Qianhui Wu, Chin-Yew Lin, Yuqing Yang, Lili Qiu
papers.citation_signal: EMNLP 2023; Microsoft; the most adopted prompt-compression library (integrated in LangChain, LlamaIndex).
papers.key_contribution: Coarse-to-fine compression with a small LM: a budget controller allocates compression across instructions, demonstrations and the question, iterative token-level compression preserves dependencies, and distribution alignment tunes the small model. Up to 20x compression with little loss on GSM8K, BBH, ShareGPT and Arxiv-March23.
papers.design_implication: Add compression as an optional pre-processing stage for demonstration and retrieved-context blocks, never for the instruction or schema; default to conservative ratios and verify on the task eval, since compression interacts with distractor and position sensitivity.

papers.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
papers.authors: Zhuoshi Pan, Qianhui Wu, Huiqiang Jiang, Menglin Xia, Xufang Luo, Jue Zhang, Qingwei Lin, Victor Rühle, Yuqing Yang, Chin-Yew Lin, H. Vicky Zhao, Lili Qiu, Dongmei Zhang
papers.citation_signal: Findings of ACL 2024; Microsoft; production successor to LLMLingua.
papers.key_contribution: Frames compression as token classification with a bidirectional encoder (XLM-RoBERTa-large / mBERT) trained on GPT-4-distilled extractive compressions; task-agnostic and faithful. 2x-5x compression, 3x-6x faster compressor than prior methods, 1.6x-2.9x end-to-end latency reduction on MeetingBank, LongBench, ZeroScrolls, GSM8K, BBH.
papers.design_implication: Prefer LLMLingua-2-style extractive compression (cheap encoder, no generation) for latency-sensitive paths; target 2x-3x by default, raise toward 5x only with eval headroom. Keep an uncompressed fallback for verification stages.

papers.title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Zhi Rui Tam, Cheng-Kuang Wu, Yi-Lin Tsai, Chieh-Yen Lin, Hung-yi Lee, Yun-Nung Chen
papers.citation_signal: Widely cited in structured-output engineering discussions; motivates the two-step reason-then-format pattern.
papers.key_contribution: Forcing JSON/XML/YAML output constraints during generation significantly degrades reasoning performance relative to free-form answers, and stricter constraints degrade more.
papers.design_implication: Do not ask the model to reason inside a JSON field. Reason in free text (or native thinking), then emit the schema in a second constrained step or via a dedicated extraction call. Vendor docs now echo this (Anthropic warns that requesting step-by-step reasoning in output fields can trigger a reasoning_extraction refusal).

papers.title: Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models (Outlines)
papers.authors: Brandon T. Willard, Rémi Louf
papers.citation_signal: The reference method behind open-source constrained decoding (Outlines, adopted in vLLM and others).
papers.key_contribution: Recasts generation as finite-state-machine transitions over a precomputed vocabulary index so regex and context-free grammars constrain sampling with negligible per-token overhead, guaranteeing output structure for any model.
papers.design_implication: For self-hosted models, use FSM/grammar-constrained decoding rather than retry-on-parse-failure; precompile and cache grammars per schema, exactly as the hosted APIs (Claude structured outputs, OpenAI Structured Outputs) do.

papers.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
papers.authors: Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi, Shailesh Mishra, Christoph Endres, Thorsten Holz, Mario Fritz
papers.citation_signal: The defining indirect prompt-injection paper; hundreds of citations and the basis of OWASP LLM Top-10 guidance.
papers.key_contribution: Introduces indirect prompt injection via retrieved data, a taxonomy of impacts (data theft, worming, information-ecosystem contamination), and demonstrations against Bing Chat and code-completion engines; argues that LLM apps blur the line between data and instructions and that effective mitigations are lacking.
papers.design_implication: Every retrieved passage, tool result, log line or document in the prompt is untrusted data. Mark provenance, instruct the model never to follow instructions found inside data blocks, run a separate injection classifier on retrieved text, and keep privileged actions behind tool permissions rather than prompt text.

papers.title: Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques For Language Models (PromptInject)
papers.authors: Fábio Perez, Ian Ribeiro
papers.citation_signal: First systematic prompt-injection study; hundreds of citations; coined goal hijacking and prompt leaking.
papers.key_contribution: PromptInject composes adversarial prompts and shows that simple handcrafted inputs reliably cause goal hijacking (task redirection) and prompt leaking (exposing hidden instructions) in GPT-3, exploitable by low-skill attackers.
papers.design_implication: Assume system prompts can leak and user turns can hijack. Keep secrets out of prompts, place instructions after untrusted content as well as before, and include goal-hijack test cases in the component's regression suite.

papers.title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
papers.authors: Keegan Hines, Gary Lopez, Matthew Hall, Federico Zarfati, Yonatan Zunger, Emre Kiciman
papers.citation_signal: Microsoft production defense; the most cited prompt-level mitigation for indirect injection.
papers.key_contribution: Spotlighting transforms untrusted input to signal provenance (delimiting, datamarking with interleaved marker tokens, or encoding such as base64) and instructs the model to never follow instructions inside marked text. Reduces attack success rate from above 50% to below 2% on GPT-family models with minimal task impact.
papers.design_implication: Implement datamarking as the default wrapper for retrieved and tool-returned text (a cheap transform), with an explicit system instruction describing the marker. Pair with XML provenance tags so the same wrapper serves both injection defense and the vendor-recommended document structure.

papers.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
papers.authors: Eric Wallace, Kai Xiao, Reimar Leike, Lilian Weng, Johannes Heidecke, Alex Beutel
papers.citation_signal: OpenAI; the training-time basis for system > developer > user > tool privilege in current API models.
papers.key_contribution: Defines an explicit priority order among system, user and third-party (tool/retrieved) instructions and a data-generation method teaching models to ignore lower-privilege instructions that conflict; substantially improves GPT-3.5 robustness to injections and jailbreaks, including unseen attack types, with small capability cost.
papers.design_implication: Put policy and immutable constraints in the system/developer channel, task text in the user channel, and all retrieved or tool content in clearly delimited data blocks; never paste untrusted data into the system prompt. The component's message builder should enforce this channel discipline programmatically.

papers.title: Universal Self-Consistency for Large Language Model Generation
papers.authors: Xinyun Chen, Renat Aksitov, Uri Alon, Jie Ren, Kefan Xiao, Pengcheng Yin, Sushant Prakash, Charles Sutton, Xuezhi Wang, Denny Zhou
papers.citation_signal: Google DeepMind; the standard extension of self-consistency to free-form generation, widely adopted in agent frameworks.
papers.key_contribution: Instead of majority voting on extracted answers, the LLM is shown all sampled candidates and asked to select the most consistent one. Matches standard SC on math, matches execution-based voting on code without running code, and improves open-ended QA and long-context summarization where voting is impossible.
papers.design_implication: Use USC as the aggregator for free-form engineering outputs (incident summaries, requirement rewrites, design rationales) where exact-match voting fails; it is a single extra call over N samples and composes with the answer-verification component.

papers.title: Prompting best practices (Claude developer documentation)
papers.authors: Anthropic
papers.citation_signal: Authoritative vendor guidance that defines the state of practice for Claude models; consolidates the former per-technique pages.
papers.key_contribution: Guidance verified on the live page: be clear and direct with explicit output constraints and numbered steps; add context/motivation ('Claude is smart enough to generalize from the explanation'); 3-5 relevant, diverse examples wrapped in <example>/<examples> tags; consistent, nested XML tags (<instructions>, <context>, <input>, <document index>); roles in the system prompt for focus and tone; long context: put long documents at the top above the query (up to 30% better responses on complex multi-document inputs), wrap each in <document> with <source> and <document_content>, and ask for relevant quotes first; format control by stating what to do rather than what not to do; prefer general 'think thoroughly' instructions over prescriptive step lists when thinking is on; multishot examples shape thinking; ask for a self-check against test criteria (except on models that over-verify); explicit chaining remains useful to inspect intermediate outputs, most commonly draft -> review -> refine; prerequisites are defined success criteria and empirical tests.
papers.design_implication: Adopt the XML-tagged message layout as the component's canonical template (documents first, query last, examples in tags), make 'quote first' a toggle for grounded tasks, and switch CoT elicitation off in favor of native thinking/effort settings when the target model supports them. Treat evals as a prerequisite to any prompt change.

papers.title: Structured outputs (Claude developer documentation)
papers.authors: Anthropic
papers.citation_signal: Authoritative vendor reference for schema-guaranteed output on Claude.
papers.key_contribution: Two modes: JSON outputs via output_config.format (json_schema) and strict tool use (strict: true). Schemas are compiled to grammars for constrained decoding, so no retry loops are needed; compiled grammars cache for 24 hours; supported subset excludes recursive schemas, numeric bounds and string-length limits; limits of 20 strict tools and 24 optional parameters; best practices: make properties required, flatten nesting, check stop_reason for refusal or max_tokens, compare enums case-insensitively, and do not request step-by-step reasoning inside output fields.
papers.design_implication: The component's schema layer should normalize user schemas into the supported subset (move unsupported constraints to descriptions and validate locally), keep the reasoning outside the schema, and reuse schemas across requests to benefit from grammar caching.

papers.title: Reasoning best practices (OpenAI developer documentation)
papers.authors: OpenAI
papers.citation_signal: Authoritative vendor guidance for o-series reasoning models.
papers.key_contribution: Keep prompts simple and direct; do not add chain-of-thought instructions (they can hurt); use delimiters (markdown, XML, section titles); try zero-shot first and add examples only for complex output requirements; set explicit constraints and success criteria; use reasoning models as planners and smaller models as executors. Reported customer numbers: judge F1 0.12 -> 0.74 (Braintrust), hard image classification 50% -> 88% (SafetyKit), 4x end-to-end improvement (Blue J).
papers.design_implication: Model-tier dispatch: the same task prompt should compile to a different concrete prompt for reasoning models (no CoT trigger, few or no shots, explicit success criteria) than for non-reasoning models (CoT + examples). The planner/executor split aligns with the task decomposition component.

papers.title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
papers.authors: OpenAI
papers.citation_signal: Industry-defining release; set the expectation of 100% schema adherence via constrained decoding.
papers.key_contribution: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 with Structured Outputs scored 100% on complex JSON-schema-following evals versus under 40% for gpt-4-0613; available via strict function calling and response_format json_schema; implemented by constrained decoding; known limits include first-request latency for schema compilation, surfaced refusals, and no parallel function calls in strict mode.
papers.design_implication: Prompt-based JSON coaxing is obsolete where constrained decoding exists; the component should always prefer API-level schema enforcement and keep a parser-with-repair fallback only for models that lack it.

papers.title: The Power of Prompting (Medprompt companion blog)
papers.authors: Microsoft Research (Eric Horvitz, Harsha Nori et al.)
papers.citation_signal: Official explainer for Medprompt with the published ablation ladder.
papers.key_contribution: Publishes the MedQA ablation: zero-shot 81.7, random few-shot 83.9, +CoT 87.3, kNN few-shot + CoT 88.4, +choice-shuffle ensemble 90.2; reports SOTA across MMLU medical subsets and out-of-domain exams (electrical engineering, ML, law, accounting, NCLEX).
papers.design_implication: Use this ladder as the component's default escalation policy: start zero-shot, add retrieved exemplars, add generated rationales, add ensembling only when needed; each rung has a measured marginal gain to justify its cost.

techniques.name: Model-tier-aware reasoning elicitation (CoT / zero-shot CoT / native thinking)
techniques.description: Given a task prompt and target model descriptor, choose the reasoning mode: (a) for non-reasoning models, append a zero-shot trigger (default 'Let's think step by step' or a searched trigger such as 'Take a deep breath and work on this problem step-by-step') and use a two-stage call: stage 1 produces free-form reasoning, stage 2 extracts the final answer (Kojima pattern); if exemplars exist, prepend 3-8 few-shot CoT exemplars (Wei et al. used 8). (b) For models with native thinking (Claude adaptive thinking, OpenAI o-series), remove CoT triggers and step lists, give general instructions ('think thoroughly'), explicit constraints and success criteria, and control depth via effort/budget parameters. In both cases, place the final answer in a delimited <answer> tag or a separate schema-constrained extraction call so reasoning text never enters the structured output.
source_titles: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
Prompting best practices (Claude developer documentation)
Reasoning best practices (OpenAI developer documentation)
Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
techniques.when_to_use: Any multi-step task (root-cause analysis, requirement consistency checks, code reasoning, standards interpretation). Skip for trivial lookups or classification where latency dominates and evals show no gain (the Prompt Report found zero-shot CoT hurt gpt-3.5-turbo on MMLU).
techniques.tradeoffs: 2-5x output tokens and latency versus direct answering; on reasoning models explicit CoT instructions can reduce quality and waste tokens; long reasoning increases exposure to distractors. Quality gains are largest on arithmetic/symbolic/logical tasks and on larger models.
techniques.default_parameters: Non-reasoning models: zero-shot trigger on, two-stage answer extraction, T=0 for the single-path case; 3-5 CoT exemplars when available (Anthropic recommends 3-5 examples; Wei used 8). Reasoning models: no trigger, zero-shot first, effort medium, add 1-2 examples only for format. Always emit answer in <answer> tags or via a schema call.

techniques.name: Self-consistency and Universal Self-Consistency (sample-and-aggregate)
techniques.description: Sample N independent reasoning paths at temperature T (same prompt), extract a normalized final answer from each, and return the plurality answer; report agreement ratio as a confidence signal. For free-form outputs (summaries, rewritten requirements, code), replace voting with Universal Self-Consistency: a single aggregator call is shown all N candidates and asked to pick the most consistent one (optionally with the task criteria). Medprompt's variant additionally perturbs answer-option order per sample to cancel position bias.
source_titles: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
Universal Self-Consistency for Large Language Model Generation
Can Generalist Foundation Models Outcompete Special-Purpose Tuning? Case Study in Medicine (Medprompt)
Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
techniques.when_to_use: High-stakes answers with a checkable final value (numeric specs, pass/fail compliance judgments, root-cause selection), noisy or distractor-heavy contexts (Shi et al. show SC mitigates irrelevant-context degradation), and whenever agreement ratio is needed as a confidence input for the verification component.
techniques.tradeoffs: Cost and latency scale linearly with N (parallelizable, so latency is bounded by one call if the parallelization component fans out). Gains saturate quickly; voting needs an answer normalizer; USC adds one extra long-context call. Does not fix systematic (shared) errors.
techniques.default_parameters: N=5 by default, N=10 for quality-critical paths (Wang et al.: 5-10 paths capture most of the 40-path gain); T=0.7 (PaLM/GPT-3 setting; 0.5 for smaller models); escalate to N=10-20 only when agreement < 0.6. Medprompt ensemble: 5 runs with shuffled choices. Use USC when answers cannot be string-normalized.

techniques.name: Retrieval-based demonstration selection with order control and calibration
techniques.description: Maintain an exemplar store of solved (input, rationale, output) triples with embeddings. At inference: (1) retrieve the top-k exemplars by embedding similarity to the query (kNN); (2) optionally generate rationales for them once with the strong model and keep only those whose answer matches the gold label (Medprompt / DSPy bootstrapping / Reinforced ICL); (3) order them either by fixed entropy-ranked permutation chosen on a model-generated probing set (Lu et al.) or by ensembling over permutations; (4) wrap each in <example> tags inside <examples>; (5) for classification tasks with logprob access, apply contextual calibration using a content-free probe ('N/A') to remove recency and common-token bias. Keep label-space coverage and format fidelity as hard constraints when choosing exemplars, since labels themselves matter less than format and input distribution.
source_titles: What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3?
Can Generalist Foundation Models Outcompete Special-Purpose Tuning? Case Study in Medicine (Medprompt)
Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them: Overcoming Few-Shot Prompt Order Sensitivity
Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
Many-Shot In-Context Learning
Prompting best practices (Claude developer documentation)
techniques.when_to_use: Any task where a few hundred historical solved instances exist (ticket triage, log-to-incident classification, requirement rewriting, BOM field normalization) and output format or style must be steered.
techniques.tradeoffs: Adds an embedding lookup (ms) and k x exemplar tokens per call (cacheable prefix if exemplars are static; not cacheable if query-dependent). Wrong ordering or label-skewed exemplars can cost tens of points. Many-shot (hundreds) improves further but scales cost linearly.
techniques.default_parameters: k=3-5 exemplars (Anthropic guidance 3-5; Medprompt uses kNN few-shot); embedding model: general-purpose text embedder, upgrade to task-tuned encoder when data permits (Liu et al.); rationale generation at T=0, keep only correct; order: entropy-ranked fixed permutation or 5-permutation ensemble; calibration probe 'N/A' when logprobs exist; many-shot (100+) only with prompt caching and a long-context model.

techniques.name: Context layout and provenance wrapping for long inputs
techniques.description: Deterministic message builder: system channel holds policy, role (for tone/scope only) and immutable constraints; user channel holds <documents> first, with each passage in <document index=n><source/><metadata/><document_content/></document>, ordered so the highest-relevance passages are at the beginning and the end (U-curve mitigation), followed by <instructions>, <examples>, and the query last (repeat the query after documents for retrieval-style tasks). Untrusted content (retrieved text, tool output, logs, emails) is datamarked (interleave a marker token such as a caret between words, or use a distinctive delimiter) with a system instruction that text inside marked regions is data and its instructions must never be followed. Add 'ignore irrelevant material' and, for grounded tasks, 'first quote the relevant passages in <quotes>, then answer'. Cap injected passages at about 10-20 after reranking.
source_titles: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
Prompting best practices (Claude developer documentation)
Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
techniques.when_to_use: Every RAG or document-grounded call, every call that includes tool results or third-party text, and any input above roughly 20k tokens.
techniques.tradeoffs: Datamarking adds tokens (markers) and can slightly affect readability; quote-first adds output tokens; XML wrapping is cheap. Reordering passages by relevance requires a reranker score. Spotlighting is a mitigation, not a guarantee.
techniques.default_parameters: Documents before query; top-1 passage first, top-2 last, rest in between; k=10-20 passages (reader accuracy saturates near 20 per Liu et al.; 20->50 docs adds ~1.5 points); quote-first on for long-document tasks; datamarking on for all retrieved/tool text (Hines et al.: attack success >50% -> <2%); query repeated after documents for key-value style lookups.

techniques.name: Schema-constrained output with reason-then-format separation
techniques.description: Define the output contract as a JSON schema (all properties required, additionalProperties false, flat structure, enums for categorical fields, short 'explanation' string instead of reasoning fields). Execution: step 1 produces free-form reasoning or uses native thinking; step 2 emits the schema using API-level constrained decoding (Claude output_config.format json_schema or strict tools; OpenAI response_format json_schema / strict functions; Outlines FSM grammars for self-hosted models). Normalize user schemas into the vendor-supported subset (move minimum/maximum/minLength to descriptions and validate locally), reuse schemas verbatim to hit grammar caches, check stop_reason for refusal/max_tokens, and compare enums case-insensitively. Fallback for models without constrained decoding: parser with one repair call.
source_titles: Structured outputs (Claude developer documentation)
Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models (Outlines)
Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
techniques.when_to_use: Any output consumed by code: extraction from specs, BOM/CAD metadata normalization, test-log classification, incident fields, tool arguments, and all inter-stage handoffs within the pipeline.
techniques.tradeoffs: First use of a schema adds compilation latency (cached ~24h on Claude); strict mode may disable parallel tool calls on some vendors; unsupported schema features return 400s; forcing reasoning into the schema degrades quality (Tam et al.). Two-step adds one call but preserves accuracy.
techniques.default_parameters: Always two-step when the task needs reasoning; one-step constrained decode for pure extraction. Schema: required-all, flat, <=24 optional params, enums for labels, 'explanation' max about 2 sentences. Grammar reuse: identical schema objects per task version. Fallback repair attempts: 1.

techniques.name: Automatic prompt optimization (APE / OPRO / DSPy-MIPRO / TextGrad) over a declared signature
techniques.description: Represent every pipeline stage as a signature (typed inputs/outputs, metric). Optimization loop: (1) build a dev set (hundreds of examples; OPRO used ~260 GSM8K training items) and a disjoint test set; (2) propose candidate instructions with an LLM at T=1.0 (APE: 50-64 candidates from demos; OPRO: 8 new per step conditioned on the top-20 (instruction, score) history plus 3 exemplars); (3) score with the target model at T=0 on the dev set using execution accuracy or the task metric; (4) jointly bootstrap demonstrations by running the program and keeping traces that pass the metric (DSPy BootstrapFewShot: max_bootstrapped_demos=4, max_labeled_demos=4; RandomSearch: num_candidate_programs=10; MIPROv2 Bayesian search with auto light/medium for 200+ examples); (5) for LLM-judged objectives, use TextGrad-style textual gradients: a critic produces structured critiques, an editor applies them to the instruction; (6) run a format sweep (10-20 FormatSpread variants) on the winner; (7) freeze, version, and store the compiled prompt keyed by (task_id, model_id).
source_titles: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers (APE)
Large Language Models as Optimizers (OPRO)
DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines
Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs (MIPRO)
TextGrad: Automatic 'Differentiation' via Text (journal version: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback)
Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (FormatSpread)
The Prompt Report: A Systematic Survey of Prompt Engineering Techniques
techniques.when_to_use: Whenever a stage has a measurable metric and at least ~10 labeled examples; mandatory on model upgrades (prompts and orderings do not transfer across models) and when a human has spent more than a few hours hand-tuning.
techniques.tradeoffs: Optimization cost is a few cents to tens of dollars and minutes to hours (DSPy docs: typical run about $2, ten minutes); overfitting risk with small dev sets (MIPROv2 recommended at 200+ examples); optimized prompts can be opaque ('Take a deep breath'); requires an eval harness, which is the real engineering cost.
techniques.default_parameters: Dev set 100-300, test set disjoint; APE 50 candidates, no iteration; OPRO top-20 history, 8 proposals/step, 3 exemplars, optimizer T=1.0, scorer T=0, ~20-50 steps; DSPy: ~10 examples -> BootstrapFewShot (4 bootstrapped + 4 labeled demos), 50+ -> RandomSearch (10 candidates), 200+ -> MIPROv2 auto=light/medium; format sweep 10-20 variants; re-optimize on every model change.

techniques.name: Task-agnostic reasoning scaffolds: Self-Discover structures and meta-prompting conductors
techniques.description: On first sight of a new task type, run a planning call (Self-Discover): SELECT relevant atomic reasoning modules from a fixed library of ~39 (critical thinking, step decomposition, assumption checking, constraint satisfaction, analogy, etc.), ADAPT them to the task description, IMPLEMENT them as a JSON reasoning structure (ordered keys with empty values). Cache the structure keyed by a task signature hash and reuse it for every instance by asking the model to fill it in. For complex compound tasks, use the meta-prompting conductor: a task-agnostic conductor prompt decomposes the task, generates tailored expert instructions, dispatches each to a fresh-context expert call (optionally with a code interpreter), then integrates and explicitly verifies before answering.
source_titles: Self-Discover: Large Language Models Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
Meta-Prompting: Enhancing Language Models with Task-Agnostic Scaffolding
Principled Instructions Are All You Need for Questioning LLaMA-1/2, GPT-3.5/4
techniques.when_to_use: When the component receives a natural-language task it has not seen before and must decide how to execute it; when a task mixes heterogeneous skills (e.g., read a standard, inspect code, compute a tolerance); as the cheap alternative to heavy self-consistency.
techniques.tradeoffs: One extra planning call per task type (amortized); structures may be suboptimal for rare instances; conductor pattern multiplies calls by the number of experts and needs a verification step to avoid integrating wrong expert outputs. Self-Discover reported 10-40x less compute than CoT-SC with higher accuracy.
techniques.default_parameters: Module library of 39 seed modules (Self-Discover); planning call at T=0 with the strongest available model; structure cache TTL tied to task version; conductor: max 5 experts per task, fresh context per expert, mandatory verify step, code interpreter enabled for numeric/logic sub-tasks; apply the 26-principle linter (explicit task statement, audience, delimiters, output primer) to every generated expert instruction.

techniques.name: Prompt compression for demonstration and context blocks
techniques.description: Before the final call, pass the demonstration and retrieved-context blocks (never the system policy, schema or query) through an extractive compressor. LLMLingua-2 style: a bidirectional encoder classifies each token keep/drop with a target ratio; LLMLingua style: a budget controller allocates ratio across sections, then iterative token-level perplexity-based dropping with a small causal LM. Re-insert provenance markers after compression, and run the task eval at each ratio before enabling in production. Skip compression entirely when the prefix is served from a prompt cache (compression destroys cache hits) or when a verifier stage needs verbatim text.
source_titles: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
techniques.when_to_use: Long, repetitive context (meeting-style logs, test output, verbose specs) on cost- or latency-sensitive paths where prompt caching does not apply (query-dependent context).
techniques.tradeoffs: Adds a compressor pass (encoder: ms; causal LM: tens to hundreds of ms); risk of dropping the one decisive token (part numbers, thresholds), so numeric/identifier spans should be protected; interacts with position effects; invalidates cache prefixes.
techniques.default_parameters: Target ratio 2x-3x by default, up to 5x with eval headroom (LLMLingua-2 range 2-5x; LLMLingua up to 20x only for CoT exemplars); protect identifiers, numbers, units and code tokens from dropping; compress demonstrations before documents; disable when cache hit rate > 50%.

architecture_recommendations: 1. Make the unit of configuration a Signature, not a prompt string: {inputs with types and provenance class, outputs as JSON schema, task description, success metric, domain hints}. Concrete prompts are compiled artifacts derived from a Signature plus a Model Profile, stored and versioned as (signature_version, model_id, compiled_prompt, eval_scores). This mirrors DSPy/MIPRO and makes the component pluggable under any pipeline stage.

2. Implement a Model Profile registry that drives technique selection: reasoning-native (no CoT trigger, zero-shot first, effort/budget control, native structured outputs) versus standard (zero-shot CoT or few-shot CoT, two-stage answer extraction, constrained decoding if available, otherwise parse+repair). Anthropic and OpenAI docs both show that the right prompt differs by tier; a single prompt for all models is a documented anti-pattern.

3. Build a deterministic Message Builder enforcing channel discipline (system = policy and immutable constraints; user = documents first, then instructions, examples, query last; data blocks datamarked and XML-tagged with provenance). This single module encodes Lost-in-the-Middle ordering, Anthropic long-context guidance, spotlighting and instruction-hierarchy rules so every other component inherits them.

4. Expose a Task Planner that, for an unseen natural-language task, runs one Self-Discover-style planning call to produce a reasoning structure and an execution plan (which techniques to enable: SC N, exemplar k, quote-first, schema), caches it by task-signature hash, and lets humans edit the plan as config. This is how the component 'reasons about how to execute' at amortized cost.

5. Ship a Technique Registry organized by the Prompt Report taxonomy (zero-shot, few-shot/ICL, thought generation, ensembling, decomposition, self-criticism) with each technique as a strategy object exposing cost/latency estimates. The orchestrator composes them per the Medprompt escalation ladder: zero-shot -> kNN exemplars -> generated rationales -> SC/ensemble, stopping when the eval target is met.

6. Treat demonstrations as data infrastructure: an Exemplar Store with embeddings, bootstrapped rationales filtered by metric, fixed entropy-ranked ordering per model, and label-space coverage checks. Reuse the hybrid-retrieval index technology for exemplar kNN.

7. Separate reasoning from formatting at the API boundary: every stage returns {reasoning_text or thinking handle, structured_output validated against schema, confidence (SC agreement or USC rationale), citations/quotes}. Use vendor constrained decoding; normalize schemas into the supported subset; keep one repair retry as fallback.

8. Make evaluation a first-class dependency: the component refuses to promote a compiled prompt without a dev/test split, reports FormatSpread-style intervals over 10-20 format variants, and runs an injection regression suite (goal hijack, prompt leak, indirect injection in retrieved text). Re-optimization is triggered automatically by model_id change.

9. Provide an Optimizer Service with budget presets (light: APE 50 candidates or BootstrapFewShot; medium: OPRO 20 steps or RandomSearch 10 candidates; heavy: MIPROv2/TextGrad with 200+ examples), running against the stage's metric, writing results back to the prompt registry with full lineage.

10. Domain adaptation through configuration only: a Domain Pack supplies vocabulary/glossary, units and identifier regexes to protect from compression, exemplar corpora, output schemas, and domain verifier hooks (compilers, test runners, units checkers). The prompting logic itself stays domain-agnostic, exactly as Medprompt and Self-Discover demonstrate transfer across medicine, engineering and law.

11. Observability: log the fully rendered prompt hash, model_id, technique flags, token counts by block (system/docs/examples/query/output), SC agreement, schema-validation outcome, refusal/stop reasons, and injection-classifier scores, so cost and quality can be attributed to individual techniques.

12. Safety defaults: personas only for tone and scope; no secrets in prompts (prompt leaking is trivial); never place retrieved text in the system channel; every self-check must consume an external signal (tests, schema, evidence) per Huang et al.; privileged actions gated by tool permissions, not prompt text.
pitfalls: Order sensitivity of few-shot demonstrations: identical examples in different orders range from near-random to SOTA (Lu et al., ACL 2022). Mitigate with entropy-ranked fixed ordering on a model-generated probe set or permutation ensembling; re-select on every model change because orderings do not transfer.

Formatting brittleness: whitespace, separators and casing alone shift accuracy by up to 76 points (Sclar et al., ICLR 2024). Mitigate by freezing canonical templates, treating any template edit as a code change, and reporting eval intervals over 10-20 format variants.

Label and recency bias in few-shot classification: models favor answers appearing late in the prompt or common in pretraining (Zhao et al., ICML 2021). Mitigate with contextual calibration (content-free probe), balanced label order, and shuffled-choice ensembling (Medprompt).

Lost in the middle: gold evidence in the middle of 20 passages drops GPT-3.5-Turbo from 75.8% to 53.8%, below the closed-book baseline (Liu et al., TACL 2024). Mitigate by reranking, placing top evidence first and last, capping at 10-20 passages, and repeating the query after documents.

Distraction by irrelevant context: adding irrelevant sentences dramatically lowers reasoning accuracy (Shi et al., ICML 2023). Mitigate with tighter retrieval, 'ignore irrelevant information' instructions, quote-first grounding and self-consistency.

Zero-shot CoT is not universally beneficial: in the Prompt Report MMLU benchmark zero-shot CoT underperformed plain zero-shot on gpt-3.5-turbo, and vendor docs say CoT instructions can hurt reasoning models. Mitigate by making reasoning elicitation an evaluated, model-tier-specific setting.

Persona prompts do not improve objective accuracy and their effects are unpredictable (Zheng et al., Findings EMNLP 2024). Mitigate by using roles only for tone and scope and not spending optimization budget on persona search.

Intrinsic self-correction can degrade answers (Huang et al., ICLR 2024). Mitigate by grounding every review step in external signals: test execution, schema validation, retrieved evidence, or an independent verifier with different context.

Format restriction degrades reasoning when the model must reason inside JSON (Tam et al. 2024); Anthropic additionally warns that requesting step-by-step reasoning in output fields can cause a reasoning_extraction refusal. Mitigate with reason-then-format two-step calls.

Prompt injection (direct and indirect) remains unsolved at the model level (Perez & Ribeiro 2022; Greshake et al. 2023). Mitigate with spotlighting/datamarking of untrusted text (>50% -> <2% attack success in Hines et al.), instruction-hierarchy channel discipline, injection classifiers, least-privilege tools, and a regression suite of hijack and leak attacks.

Manual prompt engineering is slow and unexplainable: the Prompt Report's expert spent 47 steps (~20 hours) to reach F1 0.53 with unexplained sensitivities (duplicated text raised F1; anonymizing names lowered it 0.08), and was beaten by an automatically compiled prompt (0.548). Mitigate by investing in evals and automatic optimization instead of long manual loops.

Optimized prompts overfit small dev sets and do not transfer across models (OPRO/APE results are model-specific; DSPy docs warn MIPROv2 overfits below ~200 examples). Mitigate with disjoint test sets, re-optimization on model change, and budget presets matched to data size.

Prompt compression can drop decisive tokens (part numbers, thresholds) and destroys prompt-cache prefixes. Mitigate with identifier protection, conservative 2-3x ratios, per-task evals and disabling compression on cached prefixes.

Structured-output limits: unsupported schema features (recursion, numeric bounds, string lengths on Claude) return 400s; first-use grammar compilation adds latency; strict mode may disable parallel tool calls; refusals still bill. Mitigate by schema normalization, schema reuse for cache hits, stop_reason handling and max_tokens headroom.

Over-prompting frontier models: prescriptive step lists, 'if in doubt use tool' defaults and legacy verification instructions cause over-thinking, over-verification and subagent overuse on newer Claude models (Anthropic best-practices page). Mitigate by tuning instructions per model and using effort settings rather than more prompt text.
evaluation_metrics: Task accuracy / exact match / F1 on a held-out test set per stage, reported as an interval across 10-20 semantically equivalent prompt formats (FormatSpread) rather than a point estimate.
Self-consistency agreement ratio and its calibration (ECE / reliability curve of agreement vs correctness) as the confidence signal handed to the verification component.
Position-robustness curve: accuracy as a function of gold-evidence position and number of passages (Lost-in-the-Middle protocol), tracked per model.
Distractor robustness: accuracy delta between clean and irrelevant-context-augmented inputs (GSM-IC style) for the domain's own tasks.
Demonstration sensitivity: accuracy variance across k random exemplar orderings and across exemplar subsets before and after order fixing.
Schema adherence rate (parse success without repair), repair-retry rate, refusal rate and max_tokens truncation rate for structured outputs.
Prompt-injection attack success rate on a regression suite covering goal hijacking, prompt leaking and indirect injection in retrieved text, measured with and without spotlighting.

Cost and latency per technique: tokens by prompt block (system/docs/examples/query/output), calls per task, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, and marginal accuracy gain per added rung of the escalation ladder (zero-shot -> kNN -> CoT -> ensemble).
Optimization efficiency: dev-vs-test gap of compiled prompts (overfitting), optimization spend in dollars and wall-clock, and improvement over the human baseline prompt.
Grounding fidelity for RAG prompts: citation precision (quoted spans actually in context), unsupported-claim rate, and faithfulness judged by an independent verifier.
Compression safety: accuracy retention at each compression ratio and rate of dropped protected tokens (identifiers, numbers, units).
engineering_adaptation_notes: Code: use execution-based signals (tests, compilers, linters) as the optimization metric and the verifier; Universal Self-Consistency matches execution-based voting when execution is unavailable; keep code outputs out of JSON reasoning fields and return them in fenced blocks or dedicated schema strings; constrained decoding can enforce language grammars for DSLs (Outlines FSM).

Specifications and standards documents: wrap each clause/section in <document index source section_id> tags, place the most relevant clauses first and last, cap at 10-20 clauses, and require quote-first grounding so answers cite clause IDs; use the two-step pattern to reason about applicability then emit a schema {clause_id, applies, rationale, confidence}.

Requirements: exemplar store of accepted/rejected requirement rewrites gives kNN few-shot for style; Min et al. implies real in-domain inputs matter more than perfect labels, so bootstrap rationales with the model and filter by a checklist metric (atomic, verifiable, unambiguous); use USC to pick the most consistent rewrite among N samples.

Test logs and incident reports: these are long, repetitive and untrusted (may contain injected text from user-controlled fields), so apply datamarking, 'ignore irrelevant lines' instructions, and LLMLingua-2 compression with protection for identifiers, timestamps, error codes and numeric values; classify severity with calibrated few-shot prompts and shuffled label order.

CAD/BOM metadata: part numbers, units and tolerances are exactly the tokens compression and paraphrase destroy, so disable compression on these fields, enforce schemas with enums for unit systems and regex-described identifiers (described in field text since vendor schema subsets lack pattern constraints), and validate numerics locally after decoding.

Engineering standards transfer: Medprompt reported out-of-domain gains on electrical-engineering and other professional exams using only domain-agnostic techniques, and Self-Discover structures transferred across model families, so the Domain Pack should contribute vocabulary, exemplars, schemas and verifier hooks while the reasoning scaffolds stay generic.

Planner/executor split for engineering workflows: follow the OpenAI reasoning-model guidance of using a reasoning model as planner (Self-Discover structure, decomposition) and cheaper models as executors for per-item extraction, with constrained decoding on executors to keep handoffs machine-readable.

Model upgrades are routine in engineering orgs; because orderings, triggers and format rankings do not transfer across models (Lu, Sclar, OPRO), the registry must re-run the optimizer and the full eval interval on every model_id change before promotion.
composition_notes: Hybrid retrieval: the prompting component consumes the reranked passage list and owns layout (top passages first and last, k=10-20, XML provenance tags, datamarking, query repeated after documents). Retrieval should expose reranker scores so layout can be relevance-ordered; the same vector index technology serves the exemplar store for kNN demonstration selection.

Task decomposition: Self-Discover planning and meta-prompting conductors are the prompt-level realization of decomposition; the decomposition component emits sub-task Signatures, and the prompting component compiles each into a model-tier-specific prompt with its own schema, enabling planner (reasoning model) / executor (cheaper model) splits as recommended by OpenAI guidance.

Answer verification: self-consistency agreement ratio, USC selection rationale, quote citations and schema-validation outcomes are the inputs the verifier consumes; conversely, verification results (tests, evidence checks) are the external signal that makes self-check prompts valid, since intrinsic self-correction alone degrades answers (Huang et al.). Draft -> review -> refine chaining is the recommended Anthropic pattern and should be implemented as separate verifier signatures.

Parallelization: self-consistency samples, shuffled-choice ensembles, permutation ensembles, FormatSpread sweeps, APE/OPRO candidate scoring and meta-prompting experts are all independent calls; the parallelization component fans them out so latency stays near one call while the prompting component defines the aggregation (vote, USC, conductor integration).

Caching: stable prefixes (system policy, static exemplars, many-shot blocks, compiled grammars) should be laid out first so prompt caches and grammar caches hit; query-dependent kNN exemplars and retrieved documents go after the cached prefix; Self-Discover structures and compiled prompts are cached by task-signature and model_id; compression must be disabled on cached prefixes because it breaks byte-identical matching; semantic caches should key on the normalized task prompt plus technique flags, since different technique settings produce different answers.

Pipeline RAG: the end-to-end RAG pipeline is a multi-stage LM program, so MIPRO-style joint optimization of all stage prompts against the final answer metric applies directly; spotlighting and instruction-hierarchy channel discipline protect against indirect injection carried by retrieved text; quote-first grounding and 'ignore irrelevant context' instructions address distractor sensitivity; structured handoffs between stages use constrained decoding so each stage's output is a validated contract.

Prompting and architecture best practices overall: define success criteria and evals before any prompt work (Anthropic prerequisite), version compiled prompts with lineage, re-optimize on model change, and prefer configuration (Model Profiles, Domain Packs, technique flags) over prompt text edits so the system stays task-agnostic while remaining tunable for every engineering domain.
